newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - OCT 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - OCT 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Finance ministry sources say taxation of state titles is just a matter of time. Industrialists and merchants lend their voices to calls for taxation, but say concerned about timing so as to avert an increase in interest rates.
--TVX Gold sends ultimatum to the government to clear roads blocked by local residents by October 23 or it will pull out of 65 billion drachma deal.
--Trading hours to be extended on Saturdays to include evenings. Confederation of Greek Merchants calls for trading hours to be extended from 7 a.m.-9 p.m. Monday to Saturdays.
--The first segment of 2.2 million digital switches to be offered to Intracom and Siemens by telecommunications organisation, OTE. The 350,000 switches contract has a budget of 14 billion drachmas.
--Fuel price fluctuations put hopes of fall in inflation below 8.5 percent and in interest rates in danger. Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) calls for meeting with Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
--Finance ministry prepares to test the market with Monday's auction of seven-year bonds with annual interest of 12.5 percent, down from 12.7.

--Government sets up parliamentary investigatory committee to look into case of Athens casino at seaside suburb of Floisvos. --Big business, nightclubs and bars come under the tax department's microscope in efforts to increase state revenues. --New blow to domestic pharmaceutical industry as Glaxo Wellcome shuts down production.
--Aluminium of Greece brings four-day week with reduced wages and early retirement plan up for discussion with workers as part of worldwide plans to cut costs by 20 percent.
--SEB to call for increased privatisation and cutbacks in public expenditure in forthcoming meeting with prime minister.

--New form of crash convergence programme on the cards for all those countries which fail to make the grade for European economic and monetary union. The new programme will be more detailed, will be monitored annually and will provide sanctions for non-performance.

--Canada's TVX Gold's patience comes to an end and says it will pull out of 65 billion drachma deal if blockades not lifted by Tuesday. Development Minister Vasso Papandreou says government will honour its side of the contract.

--Finance ministry decides sudden fall in interest rates on state bonds to ease the public debt. Treasury bill issue at end-October will carry the same lower 12.5 interest rate. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
